reasons.A: Short, blunt declaratives mixed with medium ones ('They were rooms.', 'They have names.') and dry deadpan understatement track the passage's choppy rhythm and whimsical plainness most closely, though it lacks the passage's exclamations.
reasons.B: Catches the passage's rhetorical questions and wry humour, but its long, semicolon-laden periodic sentences are more elaborate and literary than the passage's clipped, conversational movement.
reasons.C: Smooth, even, modern-essay prose with a reflective close and figurative polish ('lifts that hum you up'); no questions, exclamations or abrupt short sentences, so it least resembles the passage's quirky, jerky voice.
